title: Copper from a current
hook: A steady current runs through copper sulfate solution for an hour. How much copper forms?

knows: that an electric current is moving charge
that a mole is a counted amount
doesNotKnow: that charge converts to a count of electrons and so to a mass of metal
that each copper ion needs a fixed two electrons

misconception: The current alone decides how much metal is deposited.
objective: The learner can work out that 2.0 A for 1.0 h is 7,200 C, about 0.0746 mol of electrons, about 0.0373 mol of copper and about 2.4 g, and that halving the current or the time halves the copper.

claims.text: A current of 1 ampere is 1 coulomb of charge per second, so the charge is current times time.
claims.source: SI definition of the ampere (BIPM SI Brochure, 9th ed.): 1 A = 1 C/s.

claims.text: One mole of electrons carries about 96,485 coulombs (the Faraday constant).
claims.source: Faraday constant F = 96,485.33 C/mol (CODATA 2018; SI exact value 96,485.332...).

claims.text: Copper(II) ions take two electrons to become a copper atom: Cu²⁺ + 2 e⁻ → Cu.
claims.source: Standard cathode half-reaction (Atkins, Physical Chemistry; CRC Handbook electrochemical series).

claims.text: The molar mass of copper is about 63.55 g/mol.
claims.source: IUPAC standard atomic weight of copper 63.546, rounded 63.55.

claims.text: 2.0 A for 1.0 h passes 7,200 C, which is about 0.0746 mol of electrons, about 0.0373 mol of copper, and about 2.4 g (2.37 g).
claims.source: Q = 2.0 × 3,600 = 7,200 C; 7,200 / 96,485 = 0.07462 mol; / 2 = 0.03731 mol; × 63.55 = 2.371 g (node; Demo.tsx grams()). Wrong options: 1.2 g (forgot the 2 electrons, i.e. halved), 4.7 g (treated 1 electron per atom).

claims.text: The other stage values: 15 min at 2.0 A gives about 0.59 g, 30 min about 1.19 g; 1 h at 1.0 A gives about 1.19 g.
claims.source: Mass is proportional to current × time: 1,800 C → 0.5926 g; 3,600 C → 1.185 g (node).

claims.text: Model: all the current goes into depositing copper (100% current efficiency).
claims.source: Stage label 'all current making copper'. Real plating baths lose a few percent to side reactions (Faraday's laws describe the ideal).

recall.question: The same cell deposits copper using 1.0 A for 2.0 h. Compared with 2.0 A for 1.0 h, the copper is…
recall.why: Charge is current times time: 1.0 × 2.0 = 2.0 A·h either way, the same count of electrons, the same copper.
